engineering.verdict: Real, tested, production software - but sitting just BELOW its own Tier P target band, and the reason is specific.

evidence_run_today.lint: npm run lint -> exit 0, no problems
evidence_run_today.typecheck: npm run typecheck -> exit 0, no errors (strict)
evidence_run_today.tests: npm test -> 1836 passed across 214 files, exit 0
evidence_run_today.build: npm run build -> exit 0, webpack production build

met: Real business-logic tests, not a smoke suite - 214 files covering suppression, send governance, per-mailbox caps, warm-up ramp, unsubscribe rails, bounce policy and reply matching, with genuine fail-closed assertions
Merge-blocking CI gate, branch protection on main
Automated deploy via Entra OIDC with a post-deploy health check, verified by commit rather than liveness
Secrets gitignored; .env.example is the committed template
Error monitoring wired (Sentry server + edge configs)
not_met: CLOSED 2026-08-27 (cycle 43) - critical journey J5 (enrol, launch, send, reply, opt-out) now has end-to-end coverage: src/server/email-sequences/j5-journey.integration.test.ts walks one prospect through all five stages against a real PostgreSQL database with the mailbox transport CAPTURED (no credential, no network - fetch is stubbed to throw). It runs merge-blocking in CI via the 'Integration tests' step of the e2e job. It is an integration test rather than a Playwright spec on purpose: e2e/env.ts blanks every provider credential so a real send is impossible, and capturing the transport needs a module boundary a built production server does not expose - the reasoning is recorded in SCOPE.md §2. PROVEN CAPABLE OF FAILING, not merely observed to pass: breaking the planner's read of Contact.isSuppressed failed it with 'expected 1 to be +0', and breaking the inbound reply-to-contact matcher failed it with "expected null to be 'itest-j5-contact'".
Coverage thresholds are NOT verified as enforced. A test:coverage script exists; whether CI fails below a threshold was not checked today, so it is not claimed.
Sentry is configured but I did not verify it is RECEIVING events in production. Wired is not the same as live.
engineering.why_not_higher: The standard is explicit that a 9 requires strict typecheck, lint, real tests AND enforced coverage, e2e on critical journeys, live error monitoring, gitignored secrets, a merge-blocking CI gate, and automated deploy plus health check - ALL present and passing. Three of those are unproven or absent. Rounding to 8.5 to land inside the tier band would be exactly the false-9 the protocol exists to prevent.
engineering.why_not_lower: 1836 genuine tests with fail-closed assertions on the send path is not a scaffold. Every gate that was run, passed.

customer_ready.status: GRADED 2026-08-23 by walking the integrate/monday-pilot build in Chromium with a real session (13 pages, all HTTP 200, zero console errors)
customer_ready.cap_note: The previous 4.0 was CAPPED for a broken core journey - production minting unsubscribe links on the app domain. That defect is fixed and tested on this branch (e61cbde), so the cap no longer applies. Every other cap was checked and none applies: no leakage (BC-01 green and proven to catch one), no customer-facing dev-isms, no placeholder content, health check and monitoring present.
customer_ready.limitation: Walked a FIXTURE database of four near-empty workspaces, not production with seventeen real clients. Strong evidence about empty states, weak about data scale. Two prior findings (Campaigns column reading 0, and the sends contradiction at production scale) could be neither confirmed nor refuted.
top_blockers: CLOSED 2026-08-27 (cycle 39) - Bounce rate was structurally pinned at 0%: MAILBOX_BOUNCE_DETECTION_ENABLED is true in production (verified by reading the App Service config, not assumed), but the mailbox NDR path suppressed the address without ever writing OutboundEmail.status = BOUNCED, which is what the metric counts. Both channels now write through src/server/email/outbound/record-bounce.ts. Red-first test shown failing before the fix. STILL OWED: the figure cannot move until live sending resumes and a real NDR arrives - prove it FIRED in production before treating this as measured. CORRECTION: the '<2% non-negotiable' in the previous wording had NO primary source - neither Google nor Microsoft publishes a bounce threshold. Google publishes a SPAM COMPLAINT limit only: below 0.10%, never above 0.30%.
The product shows two truths about one client - Overview reads "Activity - not started" while Activity reads "EMAILS SENT 1". Two sources of truth.

CLOSED 2026-08-27 (cycle 43) - the core job is now walked end to end by src/server/email-sequences/j5-journey.integration.test.ts (enrol, launch, send, reply, opt-out honoured), against a real database with a captured transport, merge-blocking in CI. STILL OWED: this is walked by a test, NOT by a human in a browser against production data. The customer-ready score is a WALKING grade and is not re-graded here - that remains queue item 10.
E-06: one mailbox on two workspaces duplicates raw inbound mail including body text.

OWED BY GREG, not by engineering - Art.28 data-processing agreements with Sentry, RocketReach and Resend. These are signatures on commercial contracts; no code change can close them, so from 2026-08-27 (cycle 43) they are recorded as a commercial action and no longer counted against the ENGINEERING grade. They still gate the customer-ready grade until signed. The line to forward to each supplier: 'We process personal data of EU/UK data subjects through your service and require a signed Article 28 GDPR data-processing agreement, including your current sub-processor list and the transfer mechanism you rely on for any processing outside the UK/EEA. Please send your standard DPA for signature.' Sentry and Resend both publish a self-serve DPA; RocketReach is the one likely to need a request through their account team.

sell_gate.result: NOT SATISFIED. Fix the lower grade first: Customer-Ready. All FOUR engineering blockers are now closed - 1 (bounce rate pinned at 0%) in cycle 39, 2 (Overview vs Activity showing two truths) and 3 (E-06 duplicate raw inbound mail) in cycle 42, and 4 (J5 end to end) in cycle 43. Blocker 5 (Art.28 DPAs) is a commercial signature, recorded as owed-by-Greg. The score is still NOT re-graded here, and that is deliberate: re-grading means WALKING the product live as a customer, not counting closed blockers, and that is queue item 10.
